classification.difficultyReason: Derive a quadratic area model from an L-shaped region and a railing constraint, then maximise it using symmetry.

content.prompt: A builder has been contracted to construct a deck for a family on the corner of their house, as shown. The contract requirements are that $BF=DE$ and $BC=CD$, the total length of railing is $BF+BC+CD+DE=30$ metres and that the deck has the maximum possible area. If $BF=x$ m and $A\text{ m}^2=\text{area of the deck}$:

spec.description: An L-shaped deck above and to the left of a rectangular house, retaining B, C, D, E, F and all five right-angle markers. House style replaces decorative blue outlines with black and omits the pale blue fill; the editable region labels distinguish deck and house.
spec.mathematics: BF and DE are equal short boundary segments; BC and CD are equal outer sides. The house occupies the lower-right corner of the outer square.
spec.answerVisibility: Only source labels and right-angle markers are supplied; no calculated dimensions or answers appear.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Construct a formula relating $A$ and $x$ with $A$ the subject.

answer.worked:
Let $BC=CD=s$ metres. The railing constraint gives
$$\begin{align*}2s+2x&=30\\s+x&=15\\s&=15-x.\end{align*}$$
The deck is the outer square minus the square occupied by the house corner. The inner square has side $(15-x)-x=15-2x$ metres.
$$\begin{align*}A&=(15-x)^2-(15-2x)^2\\A&=225-30x+x^2-(225-60x+4x^2)\\A&=30x-3x^2.\end{align*}$$

children.label: b
children.prompt: Hence, find the maximum possible area of the deck.

answer.short:
$75\text{ m}^2$.

The downward-opening area parabola has its maximum at its axis of symmetry, $x=5$.
answer.worked:
For $A=-3x^2+30x$, the axis of symmetry is
$$\begin{align*}x&=-\frac{30}{2(-3)}\\x&=5.\end{align*}$$
The parabola opens downwards, so this gives a maximum. It is feasible: the outer side is $10$ m and the inner side is $5$ m.
$$\begin{align*}A_{\max}&=30(5)-3(5)^2\\A_{\max}&=150-75\\A_{\max}&=75\text{ m}^2.\end{align*}$$
